name: Twofold ignorance (the two coverings)
description: Two beginningless coverings in each soul — one hiding the soul's own nature and qualities, the other hiding its knowledge of the Supreme; the Lord destroys the first and removes the second when he grants liberation.

equivalents.note: Same word as Advaita's avidyā, but for Dvaita a real covering removed by grace, not a superimposition on Brahman.

name: The conceit of identity with God
description: The thought 'I am Brahman / I am ever the Lord, and the world is unreal', which the texts attribute to the asuras and describe as leading to blinding darkness; it contradicts experience and scripture.
notes: Recorded as the tradition states it (polemical).

name: Hatred of Hari and his devotees
description: Hostility to Viṣṇu and to those devoted to him, through which souls fit for darkness quickly reach blinding darkness; rejecting the Supreme though the wise are present seals it.

name: Desiring what one is unfit for
description: Aspiring to an office, a form of worship or a vision of God beyond one's intrinsic fitness; the one who does so falls, even from what he had.
antidotes: serving Viṣṇu according to one's fitness

name: Acting with desire for fruits
description: Action done for its results; desirelessness, flawless service and fitness are the conditions for seeing Hari, and ritual works done for results win only the lowest grace (heaven).

name: Reliance on bare reasoning
description: Trying to know Viṣṇu by reasoning alone or by the senses, apart from the true scriptures; 'devotion to bad reasoning' (kutarka) is named among the asuras' traits.

name: False scriptures
description: Texts contrary to the true scriptures, by which Janārdana is not known; some are said to have been produced to delude.

name: Arrogance (stabdhatā)
description: Pride — especially the pride of thinking oneself Brahman — warned against in the gloss on 'tat tvam asi': 'in truth you are not that; let there be no arrogance in you'.

name: Knowing otherwise (wrong cognition)
description: Misapprehension — the real sense of 'dvaita' in the Māṇḍūkya for Madhva: the soul's wrong knowledge (of its relation to body and Lord), produced by God's will and ceasing by his will when Brahman is known.
antidotes: knowledge of Brahman; the Lord's will

name: Karma already in effect (prārabdha)
description: Karma that has begun to bear fruit; it continues to be experienced after direct knowledge until the body falls, and new karma is always being made, so karma cannot be exhausted by experience alone.
notes: The prārabdha doctrine is recorded from general Vedānta knowledge; only BSB 3.1.8 was checked.
